subject: Evexia trial: evaluation approach, ownership, and timeline (post-call recap)
body:
---Message 1/4---
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Rivera <sofia@evexiahealth.com>
Cc: Michael Brooks <mike.brooks@evexiahealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-21 10:12 -0700
Subject: Evexia trial: evaluation approach, ownership, and timeline (post-call recap)

Hi Sofia / Michael —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we have alignment before we draft the trial agreement. High-level asks below, plus two options for evaluation methodology so you can confirm which you prefer.

Summary from call:
- Business goal: reduce triage time for intake forms and flag high-priority cases for human review (target: 30% reduction in average handle time).
- Recommended scope for trial: 10k anonymized historical intakes + 2 weeks live shadow on subset of live traffic (see methods below).
- Success criteria discussed: precision/recall for high-priority flags, end-to-end latency under 200ms p95, and no more than 2% false-positive rate on critical flags.

Evaluation methods (options) — please pick one preferred approach:
A) Offline-first + validation set (lower risk, faster grading)
  - We run an offline evaluation on 10k labeled records you provide (we'll accept partial labels and help with sampling).
  - Metrics: precision@k for high-priority class, recall, and class balance drift vs baseline.
  - Acceptance gate: precision >= 0.78 and recall >= 0.65 on the labeled set.
  - Owners: Evexia provides labels & sample owner; Redwood provides eval harness and scorecard.

B) Shadow-live split (preferred by product teams that care about real traffic)
  - 2-week shadow on 10% of live traffic routed to Redwood model, deterministic logging, no user-visible changes.
  - Metric collection: model suggestions vs human decisions, latency SLOs, and downstream impact markers (escalation rate).
  - Acceptance gate: model suggestions accepted by clinicians at >= 60% in blind review and latency under SLO.
  - Owners: Evexia ops owns live routing; Redwood sets up shadow pipeline and dashboards.

Proposed timeline (rough):
- Week 0 (this week): Confirm eval method + sign trial agreement (Grace to send initial SOW/dates).
- Week 1: Data handoff + sample labeling kickoff (Evexia).
- Week 2: Offline eval run OR shadow infra prep (Redwood + Evexia).
- Week 3-4: Shadow run / offline validation and joint review.

Attachments: I attached a draft evaluation rubric and a proposed timeline.

Ask: Can you confirm which evaluation method you prefer (A or B) and a primary owner on your side for data handoff? If B, please also confirm the approximate volume of daily intake traffic so we can size the shadow.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 20-min call if easier.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
---

---Message 2/4 (reply)---
From: Sofia Rivera <sofia@evexiahealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Brooks <mike.brooks@evexiahealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-21 12:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evexia trial: evaluation approach, ownership, and timeline (post-call recap)

Hi Grace —

Thanks for the clear recap. Internal notes below and our preferences:
- We prefer option B (Shadow-live split) for highest fidelity to production signals.
- Daily intake volume: ~1,200 forms/day; 10% traffic for shadow should give ~120/day (good signal).
- Primary owner for data & routing: Michael Brooks (ops lead) — he will coordinate with our infra team to provide a sandbox route and safe replay.
- We agree with the proposed acceptance gates but would like to tweak the acceptance threshold for clinician acceptance to 65% (we believe that's needed for operational confidence).

Michael and I will review the attached rubric and will get you a signed SOW by end of week if the timelines look like what you proposed.

Two quick clarifying Qs: 1) For shadow mode, will Redwood keep logs in our VPC or stream to Redwood-hosted telemetry? 2) Can the shadow run be truncated early if we hit clear pass/fail signals?

Sofia
Head of Product, Evexia Health
sofia@evexiahealth.com
---

---Message 3/4 (internal): Forward to SE + success manager---
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Brooks <mike.brooks@evexiahealth.com>, Sofia Rivera <sofia@evexiahealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-21 14:22 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Evexia trial: evaluation approach, ownership, and timeline (post-call recap)

Team — forwarding Evexia's preference for shadow (B). Key asks: 10% traffic (~120/day), clinician acceptance target bumped to 65%, storage question re: logs, and early-stop possibility.

Neha: can you draft a shadow-run infra checklist (routing, sampling, logging, privacy redaction) and estimate cost delta for 10% routing for 2 weeks? Include whether we can keep logs in customer VPC (Evexia asked).

Karthik: please review the attached eval rubric and propose a concrete blind-review process for clinician acceptance (who runs the review, how samples are selected, how to avoid bias). Also propose an early-exit statistical rule we can include in the SOW (e.g., sequential monitoring with 80/20 split or stopping rule after N samples with z-test threshold).

Notes for SOW: we should be explicit on data residency for logs, retention period (30 days by default), and that Redwood will provide anonymized aggregated dashboards for Evexia during shadow.

Grace
---

---Message 4/4 (final confirmation)---
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Rivera <sofia@evexiahealth.com>, Michael Brooks <mike.brooks@evexiahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-28 15:34 -07:00
Subject: RE: Evexia trial: evaluation approach, ownership, and timeline (post-call recap)

Sofia / Michael —

Great — thanks for confirming option B and bump to 65% acceptance. Per internal review:
- Neha attached a short infra checklist and confirms we can run shadow with logs retained in Evexia's VPC (KMS-backed) — we will provide a small agent and config.
- Karthik proposed a blind-review protocol: randomly sample 200 shadow cases over the 2-week window, stratified by confidence buckets (high/medium/low). Early-stop rule: after each 50 reviewed samples, compute cumulative acceptance rate; stop early if lower CI bound for acceptance probability >65% (pass) or upper CI bound <50% (fail). We'll include an exact statistical procedure in SOW.

Next steps and owners (final):
- SOW & trial agreement: Grace to send draft by EOD Monday (owner: Grace).
- Infra handoff & sandbox routing: owner Michael Brooks (Evexia) / Neha to support.
- Blind review process & rubric finalization: owner Karthik Iyer (Redwood) / Michael to recruit 4 clinician reviewers.
- Data sharing & redaction checklist: owners Michael + Evexia infra team.

Attachments: evexia-eval-rubric-v1.xlsx (rubric + blind-review template), proposed-trial-timeline-evexia.pdf (detailed calendar).

If that all looks right I'll send the SOW and calendar invite for the kickoff.

Thanks — excited to get this rolling.

Best,
Grace
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
